question: How do they evaluate their resulting word embeddings?

extractive_spans: We also evaluate all five models on downstream tasks from the VecEval suite BIBREF13 , using only the tasks for which training and evaluation data is freely available: chunking, sentiment and question classification, and natural language identification (NLI). The default settings from the suite are used, but we run only the fixed settings, where the embeddings themselves are not tunable parameters of the models, forcing the system to use only the information already in the embeddings.
evidence: We also evaluate all five models on downstream tasks from the VecEval suite BIBREF13 , using only the tasks for which training and evaluation data is freely available: chunking, sentiment and question classification, and natural language identification (NLI). The default settings from the suite are used, but we run only the fixed settings, where the embeddings themselves are not tunable parameters of the models, forcing the system to use only the information already in the embeddings.

Finally, we use LV-N, LV-M, and FT to generate OOV word representations for the following words: 1) “hellooo”: a greeting commonly used in instant messaging which emphasizes a syllable. 2) “marvelicious”: a made-up word obtained by merging “marvelous” and “delicious”. 3) “louisana”: a misspelling of the proper name “Louisiana”. 4) “rereread”: recursive use of prefix “re”. 5) “tuzread”: made-up prefix “tuz”.

title: Incorporating Subword Information into Matrix Factorization Word Embeddings
answer_short: by evaluating on downstream tasks from the VecEval suite, intrinsic evaluation via word similarity and word analogy tasks, and qualitative nearest-neighbor analysis for OOV words
answer_rationale: The evaluation of word embeddings is described in multiple documents. Text 2 mentions evaluation on downstream tasks from the VecEval suite (chunking, sentiment, question classification, and NLI). Text 10 specifies intrinsic evaluation via word similarity and word analogy tasks for IV words, and Text 5 and Text 8 mention qualitative nearest-neighbor analysis for OOV words. These methods collectively form the evaluation strategy.
